title: Jabalpur Second Plate of Yaśaḥkarṇa: (Kalachuri) Year 529 (?)
html:
JABALPUR SECOND PLATE OF YASAHKARNA : (KALACHURI) YEAR 529 (?)

As stated before,17 the second copper-plate of the grant of Yaśaḥkarna discovered in the Jabalpur District has long been lost. A transcript of the text on that plate has been preserved in the Central Museum, Nagpur. The paper on which it was written has now become very brittle and some letters have been damaged. The transcript is given below, together with conjectural emendations proposed in the light of the text of the Khairha plates of the same Kalachuri king.18 For permission to include the transcript in the present Volume, I am obliged to the Curator of the Museum.

TEXT

दानुबीर२परमभट्टारकमहाराजाधिराजपरमशूर३परममाहेश्वरत्रिकलिगाधिपतिनिजभुजोपाजिताश्वपति-गजपतिनरपतिराज्यत्रयाधिपति४श्रीमहीशः कर्णदेवः५ श्रीमहादेवी महाराजपुत्रः महामंत्री महामात्यः महासामंतः महापुरोहितः महाप्रतीहारः महाक्षपटलिकः .....६ महासूयाधनिकः७ महाभांडागारिकः महाध्यक्षः एतानन्यांश्च प्रदास्यमानग्रामनिवासिजनपदां ह्याहूय८ यथाहं सन्मानयति९ बोधयति समाज्ञापयति यथा विदितमस्तु भवतां यथा सम्बत१० ५२९ माघे मासि कृष्णपक्षे दशम्यां सोमदिने उत्तरायणसंक्रान्तौ नर्मदातीर-समावासे जाउलीपत्तनपाटि११करंजाग्रामः ससीमापर्यन्तः१२ चतुराघाटविशुद्धः सजलयुतः साम्रमधूकः सगर्तोषरः सनिर्गमप्रवेशः सलवणाकरः सगोप्रचारः सज्यद्गलात्तपः१३ वृक्षारामहूदोद्यान१४तृणादिसहितः काश्यपगोत्राय काश्यपावत्सारनै ध्रुवत्रिप्रवराय वाजसनेयशाखिने भट्टश्रीभवनाम१५पौत्राय भट्टश्रीनागोपुत्राय सूत्राध्ययनसंपन्नाय हरिशम्मंणे ब्राह्मणाय१६ मातापित्रोरात्मनश्च पुण्ययशोभिवृद्धये ग्रामोयमस्माभिः शासनत्वेन संप्रदत्तः [1*] अत्र वासार्थाश्वना१७ दातुर्भवति यथा सिद्धानेता१८न्भाविनः पाथिवेन्द्राद्भूयो१९ भूयो याचते रामभद्रः [1*] सामान्योयं धर्मसेतु नृपाणां२० काले काले पालनीयो भवद्भिः२१ [॥१॥*] वहुभि२२वंसुधा भक्ता राजभिः सगरादिभिः [1*] यस्य यस्य यदा भूमिः स्तस्य२३ तस्य सदा२४ फलं(लम्)२५[॥२॥*] सुवर्णमेकं गामेकां भूमेरप्येकमंगु-लं(लम्) [1*] हरन्नरकमाप्नोति यावदाभूतसंल्लवं(वम्) [॥३॥*] तडागानां सहस्रेण अश्वमेधशतेन च [1*]गवां कोटिप्रदानेन भूमिहर्ता न शुध्यति [॥४॥*] स्वदत्तां परदत्तां वा यो हरेत वसुंधरां(राम्) [1*] स विष्टायां२६

क्रुमिर्मूत्वा पितृभिः सह मज्जति [॥५॥*] फालकृष्टां महीं दद्यात्सबीजां44 सस्यशालिनीं(नीम्) [1*] यावल्सुर्यशतं लोके तावत्स्वर्गे महीयते [॥६॥*] षष्ठि45 वर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गे वसति भूमिदः [1*] आच्छेत्ता चानुमंता च तप्ते च46 नरके वसेत47 [॥७॥*] वारिहीनेष्वरण्येषु शुष्ककोटरवासिनः [1*] कृष्णसर्पास्तु जायते ब्रह्म48देवस्वहारिणः [॥८॥*] अन्यायेन हृता भूमिरत्यायेन तु हारिता [1*] हरतो हारयन्तश्च49 [दहत्या]-सप्तमं कुलं(लम्) [॥९॥*] अस्मत्कुलक्रमगताः समुदाहरति अन्यश्च दानमिदमभ्युपमोदनीयं(यम्) [1*] लक्ष्मीश्चला सलिलवृद्वृद50वद्धरायां दानं फलं परमतः प्रतिपालनीयं(यम्)51 [॥१०॥*] प्रजाहितार्थं स्मृतयः प्रणीताः घर्मेषु विद्वान्प्रतिपालयेत [1*] यो लोभमोहाद्धरते तु ग्रामान्सोधो52 व्रजेत्दुर्गतिमाश्रु53 कष्टां(ष्टाम्)54 [॥११॥*] यानीह दत्तानि पुरा नरेद्रे दानानि55 धर्मार्थयशस्कराणि [1*] निर्माल्यवंति प्रमितानि56 तानि को नाम साधुः पुनराददीत57 [॥१२॥*] भूमि यः प्रतिगृण्हाति58 यश्च भूमि प्रयच्छति [1*] उभो तौ पुण्यकर्माणौ नियतं स्वर्गगामिनो59 [॥१३॥*] शंखो60 भद्रासन क्षेत्रं61 वराश्चा62 वरवारणाः [1*] भूमिदानस्य चिन्हा(ह्ला)नि फलमेतत्पुरंदरं63 [॥१४॥*] अस्मिन्धान्य64 परिक्षीणो यः कश्चिमृपति भवेत्65 [1*] तस्याहं हस्तलग्नोस्मि शासनं न वृत्तिक्रमेत्66 [॥१५॥*] धान्यं भूवि द्रुतमिदं67 वसुधाधिपत्यमापातमाश्रमचरो68 विषयोपभोगः [1*] प्राणास्तृणाग्रजलविन्दु69समा नराणां धर्मः सखा परमहो परलोकयाने70 [॥१६॥*] धर्मलेखि-श्रीवाक्यकल71 लिखितमिति [॥*] मंगलं महाश्री72 ॥-॥

TRANSLATION

(And he), the Paramabhattāraka, Mahārājādhirāja and Paramēśvara, the illustrious Yaśaḥkaṇadēva, the devout worshipper of Mahēśvara, the lord of Trikaliṅga, who has attained, by his arm, sovereignty over the three kings, (viṣ.), the lord of horses, the lord of elephants and the lord of men, who meditates on the feet [of . . .], having called together the illustrious Mahādēvī, the Mahārājaputra, the Mahāmantrin, the Mahāmātya, the Mahāsāmanta, the Mahāpurōhita, the Mahāpratihāra, the Mahākshapaṭalika, [the Mahāpramātrī], the Mahāśvasādhanika, the Mahābhāṇdāgārika, the Mahādhyaksha—these and other (officials) and (also) the inhabitants of the village which is to be granted, duly honours, informs and commands them (as follows):—

“Be it known to you that on (the occasion of) the Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti, on Monday73, the tenth (tithi) of the dark fortnight of the month Māgha in the year 52974, We have granted, by a charter for the increase of the religious merit and fame of Our mother and father and of Ourself, the village Karaṇjā, included in the pattalā of Jāuli and situated on the bank of the Narmadā, to the extent of its limits, with its four boundaries well-determined—together with water, together with mango and madhūka trees, together with its pits and barren land, together with (the right of) egress and ingress, together with the mines of salt, together with pastute-lands, together with fertile and marshy lands, together with groves of trees, gardens of plants, grass and so forth,—to the Brāhmaṇa Hariṣarman, the son of the Brāhmaṇa, the illustrious Nāgō, (and) grandson of the Brāhmaṇa, the illustrious Bhavanāga, who belongs to the Kāśyapa gōtra (and) the Vājasanēya tākhā, has the three pravaras Kāśyapa, Āvatsāra and Naidhruva (and) has mastered the Sūtra-works.”

In this matter (this) is the prayer of the donor:—

(Here follow sixteen benedictive and imprecatory verses.)

(This charter) has been written by the illustrious Vāchchhūka, the writer of religious documents.

May there be bliss and great prosperity !

Footnotes

1(p. 633, n. 1) Above, No. 47, l. 1.

2(p. 633, n. 2) Above, pp. 239 ff.

3(p. 633, n. 3) From the lithograph (plate xxviii) in Cunningham's A. S. I. R., Vol. XXI.

4(p. 633, n. 4) Expressed by a symbol.

5(p. 633, n. 5) Cunningham read Srimad-Gāṅgeya Deva here, but the reading is unlikely; for, the name of the ruling king does not precede the title, but follows it.

6(p. 633, n. 6) This and the following akshara may be read as nāvā, but Śrī-Manāvā gives no sense. On the other hand, the title Paramābhattāraka generally precedes Mabārājādhirāja. See, e. g., No. 48, ll. 53-4.

7(p. 633, n. 7) Two aksharas are illegible here.

8(p. 633, n. 8) As the two aksharas in the beginning of the next line are certainly śvara, it appears quite likely that the epithet paramamābēśvara occurred here. Faint traces of mābē can be seen in the lithograph.

9(p. 633, n. 9) Of these three akshāras of the royal name, only ya is certain. The following two aksharas appear to be dīva.

10(p. 633, n. 10) Two aksharas are illegible here. The second may be read as ha.

11(p. 633, n. 11) Perhaps the name of the Śīva-liṅga was Alaṅghyēśvara. This name occurs also in another record of an earlier period. See No. 25, l. 24. The following two aksharas which are gone may have been dīvā.

12(p. 633, n. 12) Two aksharas are illegible here, of which the second may be ya followed by a daṇḍa.

13(p. 633, n. 13) There are faint traces of half a dozen aksharas here. Cunningham read praṇamatī which may be correct. Compare [niṭyaṇi praṇamanti in No. 69, l. 4.

14(p. 633, n. 14) This word is completely gone.

15(p. 633, n. 15) The first figure of the date is probably 7. The second has become indistinct. The top portion of the third figure, which is clear in the lithograph, shows that the unit figure was 9.

16(p. 633, n. 16) Cunningham read Srī Dhābalamiti here, but the lithograph shows that the aksharas are completely gone. The record may have ended with the usual maṅgalaṇī mābā-śrīlp.
